A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–D. Algorithms, equations, proofs, and references can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports algorithms, proofs, and analytical distributional examples, but no original experimental, simulation, user-study, or empirical data-analysis results.

after.justification: v2 retains the theoretical treatment without adding empirical results in the main text or appendices.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–4 retain the same noise calibration, eigenspace transformations, clipping, recursion, aggregation, and initial-parameter estimation procedures.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates datasets experimentally. The analytical ellipsoid and truncated-Pareto examples remain; deleting D.2's broken Gaussian-mixture appendix pointer does not remove an actual evaluation.

E2.justification: The subsample-and-aggregate baseline and theoretical comparisons with private learners and Brown et al. remain unchanged. Neither version reports empirical comparator evaluations.

E3.justification: Neither version supplies an experimental evaluation protocol. The theoretical sample-size requirements and algorithm parameter settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The outlier analysis in Section 4.2 and distributional analyses in Appendix D are retained. No ablations, empirical robustness tests, or error analyses are added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated empirical runs, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Failure probabilities in the theoretical guarantees remain unchanged.

E6.justification: The sample-complexity comparisons, outlier bounds, and ellipsoid/Pareto conclusions are unchanged. Neither version contains experimental scores or measured outcomes.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.3 moves the privacy guarantee before the utility sample-size condition, clarifying a guarantee already stated in v1's footnote and privacy proof. This restates existing mathematics; definitions, bounds, and appendix proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same core contributions: private second-moment estimation under subsamplability, recursive preconditioning, arbitrary-accuracy guarantees, and tolerance of suitably bounded outliers.

C2.justification: The subsamplability restrictions, open question concerning beta, outlier conditions, and heavy-tail applicability remain unchanged. Removing the broken appendix pointer introduces no new substantive interpretation or limitation.

D1.justification: Pseudocode, parameter choices, and Appendix B's initialization procedures are unchanged. No implementation, hardware, runtime, or code/data access information is added.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to Kamath et al., Ashtiani and Liaw, and Brown et al. are unchanged. Bibliographic punctuation differences do not change source membership.

P1.justification: v2 clarifies Theorem 3.3's wording, expands and retitles the funding acknowledgments, updates the conference footer, and removes D.2's sentence containing an unresolved '??' reference. The overall narrative and section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Typography, spacing, and line/page breaks change modestly, including reflow of Appendix D.2 across pages 20–21. The same four algorithm displays remain, with no added or removed figures or tables.

improvement.justification: v2 presents the existing privacy guarantee more clearly in Theorem 3.3, removes a misleading unresolved appendix pointer, and provides fuller funding disclosure. These modest gains in clarity and transparency improve presentation while leaving the scientific methods, proofs, and results unchanged.
